sahneler.metin: One stray electrical pulse nearly destroyed the carrier Forrestal.
A rocket fired by itself and burst a jet's fuel tank.
But the real danger was hidden below the planes: loaded bombs.
Burning jet fuel spread right beneath them.
The bombs were old, far more heat-sensitive than expected.
After ninety-four seconds, one exploded and killed most of the fire team.
134 sailors died, and the Navy rebuilt its firefighting.
Now every carrier has deck sprinklers, and every sailor fights fire.

aciklama:
On July 29, 1967, a stray electrical pulse fired a rocket across the deck of the USS Forrestal. Jet fuel burned under old bombs that cooked off in 94 seconds.
